topic: Hawa Mahal, Jaipur's 'Palace of Winds': barely a room deep behind 953 one-way lattice windows, engineered to lean 87 degrees with no real foundation
title: Jaipur's Pink Palace Is Basically A 953-Window Screen
description: AI-narrated commentary on Hawa Mahal, Jaipur's 'Palace of Winds': a five-story pink sandstone screen that's barely a room deep behind its 953 carved windows, built in 1799 for royal women to watch the city unseen, engineered to cool itself and lean 87 degrees without a real foundation. Original commentary, not a repost of any source clip.

hook_candidates.text: Jaipur's most-photographed palace hides almost nothing behind its pink screen.
Jaipur's five-story pink palace was built to stand with no real foundation at all.
What if the most photographed palace in India barely has any rooms behind it?
In 1799, Jaipur's royal women got 953 carved windows built just so they could watch the streets without ever being seen.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who's already posted a photo in front of Hawa Mahal, because they want to reveal that famous backdrop is barely a room deep.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume Jaipur's postcard-famous pink palace is a real building full of rooms behind every window.
closing_comment: Jaipur's pink palace has 953 windows total, but that 'tallest building with no foundation' claim about it is still unverified, so does anyone actually know the source?

sources.note: Confirms 953 jharokha lattice windows, built 1799, let royal women watch the street while staying unseen.
Confirms the top floors are barely one room deep and the facade leans at 87 degrees with no conventional foundation.
Explains how carved jali lattice windows like Hawa Mahal's cool interiors via accelerated airflow (Venturi effect).
